title: Power crunch tests Asia's AI buildout
lede: The defining story of the week was electricity. In Australia, NextDC slashed its FY27 guidance after distributor Jemena suspended network works at its M3 Melbourne campus, wiping A$140 million from revenue and EBITDA forecasts and sending the stock down sharply, while Microsoft and industry groups warned that grid constraints and community opposition now threaten more than three-quarters of the A$100 billion pipeline in Sydney and Melbourne. Malaysia moved to formalise oversight of its boom, drafting a Digital Infrastructure Bill as officials projected 8.39GW of data centre demand by 2030 and Johor raced to add solar generation. Public markets delivered their own verdict: stalled IPOs, a weak debut for Seoul-based Elice and warnings from S&P Global and operators including AirTrunk signalled that capital for AI infrastructure is becoming more selective and more expensive, even as committed projects from Envision's GW-scale Galaxy Campus to SK Group's 15GW plan and Aolani's 500MW Malaysia commitment kept the buildout moving.

themes.heading: NextDC's M3 power crisis
themes.narrative: NextDC dominated the week after electricity distributor Jemena halted 66kV network works at its M3 campus in West Footscray, prompting the operator to suspend its share trading and then cut FY27 guidance by A$140 million in net revenue and underlying EBITDA. The company also paused new development projects and land acquisitions, and its shares fell about 40% as community opposition to the expansion compounded the supply delay. The episode has become the clearest APAC example of how a single grid connection can reset a listed operator's growth story.
themes.narrative_zh: NextDC主导了本周的头条：电力分销商Jemena暂停了其位于西Footscray的M3园区的66kV电网工程，迫使该运营商暂停股票交易，随后将FY27财年指引下调1.4亿澳元的净收入和基础EBITDA。公司还暂停了新开发项目和土地收购，由于社区对扩建的反对叠加供电延迟，其股价下跌约40%。这一事件已成为亚太地区最鲜明的例证，说明单个电网连接问题如何重塑一家上市运营商的增长叙事。

themes.heading: Australia's grid and backlash bind
themes.narrative: Beyond NextDC, assessments this week found that over three-quarters of planned data centres around Sydney and Melbourne — roughly A$100 billion in projected investment — are at risk from stretched power grids and local opposition, with only 23 per cent of projects publicly confirmed. Microsoft and NextDC reportedly warned the NSW government in closed-door meetings that they could shift investment to Victoria or South-East Asia. The pressure is now a stated threat to Australia's ambition of becoming a regional AI hub.
themes.heading_zh: 澳大利亚电网约束与舆论反弹
themes.narrative_zh: NextDC之外，本周的多项评估发现，悉尼和墨尔本周边规划中的数据中心中超过四分之三——预计投资约1000亿澳元——因电网紧张和地方反对而面临风险，仅有23%的项目已公开确认。据报道，Microsoft和NextDC在闭门会议中警告新南威尔士州政府，他们可能将投资转移至维多利亚州或东南亚。该压力现已成为对澳大利亚打造区域AI枢纽雄心的公开威胁。

themes.heading: Malaysia drafts rules for boom
themes.narrative: Malaysia's government agreed at a National Economic Action Council meeting chaired by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to draft a Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for Cabinet submission in 2027, following Singapore's Digital Infrastructure Act. Economy Ministry officials framed the legislation as formal oversight to steer sustainable growth, while Anwar said the country must plan capacity carefully to attract quality investment. The move comes as operators flag rising power and transmission requirements as the industry's biggest near-term concern.
themes.heading_zh: 马来西亚为行业繁荣起草监管规则
themes.narrative_zh: 马来西亚政府在总理安瓦尔·易卜拉欣主持的国家经济行动理事会会议上同意，参照新加坡的《数字基础设施法》，起草《数字基础设施（数据中心）法案》，并于2027年提交内阁审议。经济部官员将该立法定位为引导可持续增长的正式监管框架，而安瓦尔表示国家必须审慎规划容量，以吸引优质投资。此举出台之际，运营商指出不断上升的电力和输电需求已成为行业近期最大的担忧。

themes.heading: Johor's power bill comes due
themes.narrative: New estimates quantified Malaysia's constraint: Petra projects data centre peak demand in Peninsular Malaysia reaching 8.39GW by 2030, while BMI warned Johor alone could absorb over 90% of the peninsula's additional generation by 2031. In response, the Johor government is targeting about 5GW of new solar capacity by 2031, and developers are being asked to bear transmission upgrade costs. Suppliers are still winning work — Jati Tinggi secured a RM30.1 million power infrastructure contract in Kulai — but grid availability is now the binding variable.
themes.narrative_zh: 新的估算量化了马来西亚的制约：Petra预测2030年马来西亚半岛数据中心峰值需求将达到8.39GW，而BMI警告称到2031年仅柔佛州就可能吸纳半岛新增发电量的90%以上。作为应对，柔佛州政府计划到2031年新增约5GW太阳能装机容量，并要求开发商承担输电升级成本。供应商仍在赢得订单——Jati Tinggi在古来获得了一份价值3010万马币的电力基础设施合同——但电网可用性如今已成为决定性变量。

themes.heading: Markets force a reality check
themes.narrative: Investor scrutiny of AI infrastructure intensified across the region. Elice fell 33% on its Seoul debut despite a retail tranche 400 times subscribed, Singapore-based DayOne is reportedly weighing delaying or downsizing its US IPO, and AirTrunk and Iren said investors are now markedly more selective. S&P Global warned that hyperscalers likely carry more AI-linked debt than public accounts show, while NextDC moved to reassure bondholders amid jittery funding markets threatening a US$155 billion Australian pipeline.
themes.heading_zh: 市场迫使行业回归现实
themes.narrative_zh: 整个地区对AI基础设施的投资者审视正在加剧。Elice在首尔上市首日下跌33%，尽管其散户认购倍数达400倍；据报总部位于新加坡的DayOne正考虑推迟或缩减其美国IPO；AirTrunk和Iren表示投资者现在明显更加挑剔。S&P Global警告称，hyperscale企业的AI相关债务可能高于公开账目所示；而NextDC则在动荡的融资市场威胁着一个1550亿美元澳大利亚项目管线之际，采取行动安抚债券持有人。

themes.heading: Korea buildout attracts heavy capital
themes.narrative: South Korea's expansion continued to draw committed funding. SC Capital Partners and NeoAI Cloud jointly invested in a 40MW AI data centre in Pohang that has also attracted government-backed capital, while SK Group's data centre arm is in talks to help fund a US$350 billion AI buildout involving 15GW of capacity by 2030. The activity contrasts with a choppy regional IPO market, underscoring that sovereign- and corporate-backed capital is still moving even as public investors turn cautious.
themes.heading_zh: 韩国数据中心建设吸引巨额资本
themes.narrative_zh: 韩国的数据中心扩张继续吸引已承诺的资金投入。SC Capital Partners与NeoAI Cloud联合投资了位于浦项的一座40MW AI数据中心，该项目还吸引了政府背景资本；与此同时，SK集团的数据中心业务部门正在商谈为一项涉及到2030年15GW容量的3500亿美元AI建设计划提供资金支持。这些活动与区域IPO市场的波动形成鲜明对比，凸显出即使公开市场投资者转向谨慎，主权资本和企业支持的资本仍在继续流动。

title_zh: 电力紧张考验亚洲AI基础设施建设
lede_zh: 本周的核心议题是电力。在澳大利亚,NextDC 在分销商 Jemena 暂停其 M3 Melbourne 园区的电网工程后大幅下调了 FY27 业绩指引,营收和 EBITDA 预测被抹去了 1.4 亿澳元,股价随之大幅下跌;与此同时,Microsoft 和行业组织警告称,电网瓶颈与社区反对现已威胁到悉尼和墨尔本超过 1000 亿澳元项目储备中四分之三以上的项目。马来西亚着手将其蓬勃发展的行业纳入正式监管框架,正在起草《数字基础设施法案》,官员们预计到 2030 年数据中心需求将达到 8.39GW,Johor 也在竞相增加太阳能发电。公开市场则给出了自己的裁决:IPO 停滞不前、总部位于首尔的 Elice 上市表现疲软,以及 S&P Global 和 AirTrunk 等运营商发出的警告。
